name: Decorative decals/coatings on tableware
anchor: EU food-contact framework Regulation 1935/2004 with Regulation (EU) 10/2011 Annex II specific migration limits as the only element-migration instrument in the register; polymer-surface rows anchor it directly or by disclosed read-across, and metal, alloy, ceramic-glaze, vitreous-enamel and glass rows are controls because their dedicated release regimes are not yet ingested.
native_basis: element release from the glaze, enamel or glass into food or food simulant (µg/kg food)
native_basis_label: element RELEASE FROM THE GLAZE, VITREOUS ENAMEL OR GLASS NETWORK INTO FOOD OR A FOOD SIMULANT, µg/kg of food, determined by the 4 percent (v/v) acetic acid filled-article or contact-surface extraction convention used for this material family, with decoration within 20 mm of the lip determined separately. This is the glaze-and-glass RELEASE basis; it is deliberately NOT the Reg (EU) 10/2011 plastics-simulant convention, and a plastics specific migration limit is never substituted for a release limit on this family.
scope_note: The decoration itself, considered separately from the article it is applied to, because decoration is a distinct release surface with a distinct exposure route. Decoration that lies on an interior surface is a fill-contact pathway. Decoration within 20 mm of the lip is a LIP-CONTACT pathway, and decoration on the exterior body is a HAND-TO-MOUTH pathway; none of the three is represented by a fill extraction on an undecorated area. The applicable lead-and-cadmium release regime for applied decoration on tableware (EU 84/500/EEC and its amendments, the FDA compliance-policy guides on ceramicware and decorated glassware, and the Proposition 65 tableware consent judgments) is absent from the register, so the row is a control and the gap is recorded.
basis_guard: element release from the glaze, enamel or glass into food
basis_guard_note: Only an instrument expressed as specific element migration into food or a food simulant may anchor a cell on this row. The guard exists to reject the three foreign bases that surround this category and would otherwise look plausible: the FOOD basis (canned-food tin maximum levels, which limit the contents and not the article), the MATERIAL-CONTENT basis (CPSIA total lead in substrate, EU REACH Annex XVII cadmium percent-by-weight restrictions, RoHS homogeneous-material limits, Japan Notice 370 and Korea MFDS percent-by-weight lead in food-contact metals), and the ARTICLE-EXTRACTION basis of the toy regime (EU 2009/48 Annex II Part III and ASTM F963 soluble limits, which are element migration from scraped-off or coated TOY material into 0.07 M hydrochloric acid, expressed per kg of MATERIAL, not per kg of food). Any of those would fail this guard and resolve to a gap rather than publish in the wrong basis. On this control row the guard is declaratory as well as operative: it records the only basis in which a future ingested instrument would be allowed to supply this row's numbers, so that a content limit, a food limit, a water limit or a plastics specific migration limit cannot later be dropped in as this row's release ceiling. The plastics clause is deliberately absent from this guard: a Reg (EU) 10/2011 value named here would fail the guard and resolve to a gap.
method: HMTc Method v2.0 (government-limit-only): the strictest applicable sovereign maximum for this exact product form expressed as specific element migration into food or a food simulant; a disclosed read-across from the nearest applicable sovereign value in the same basis where the food-contact material family is expressly excluded from or not reached by that instrument; a substantiated not-material determination; or a control. No cell is occurrence-derived, and no cell borrows a value across a basis.

Pb.rationale: No credible sovereign release ceiling for this material family is present in the HMTc regulatory register. Glazed ceramic, vitreous enamel, glass and applied decoration are governed in the real world by a dedicated lead-and-cadmium release regime (EU Council Directive 84/500/EEC as amended by 2005/31/EC for ceramic articles, and the US FDA compliance-policy guides on lead in ceramicware and decorated glassware), and by California Proposition 65 consent judgments on tableware. None of those instruments has been ingested into data/evidence/regulatory_limits.csv, and this build refuses to substitute the plastics specific migration limits for a glaze-release limit: the two are different extractions on different material families and the substitution would be a basis conflation. The cell is a control until the release regime is ingested through the verified regulatory-fetch pathway, and the gap is recorded. Lead is the dominant pathway for this material family: lead-fluxed and lead-bisilicate glazes, lead-bearing on-glaze enamels and applied decoration, and under-fired or acid-attacked glaze surfaces all release lead into acidic food. It is the single cell where the absent release regime matters most, and the gap is recorded rather than papered over with a plastics value. This row's unit of test is the decoration colour, not the article: each colour is a separate lot, and the three exposure routes (fill, lip and hand-to-mouth) are reported separately rather than pooled.
Pb.reference_method: Release testing on the filled or contact-surface article using 4 percent (v/v) acetic acid at the article's stated use temperature and duration (the release convention used for glazed, enamelled and glass food-contact articles), ICP-MS determination in the extract, with a separate determination on any decoration lying within 20 mm of the lip or on any interior decoration.

MeHg.rationale: Methylmercury is formed by microbial methylation in aquatic food chains. A glaze, an enamel and a glass network are fired inorganic matrices with no organic carbon and no methylation pathway, and no credible sovereign sets a methylmercury requirement for any food-contact material. Total mercury remains a mandatory control on this row; methylmercury is not material and never substitutes for it.
MeHg.reference_method: Total-mercury release determination per the tHg control; reflex methylmercury speciation only where total mercury is detected in the acid extract.
MeHg.regulatory_basis: No credible sovereign sets a methylmercury requirement for a ceramic, enamelled or glass food-contact article in any basis. A fired inorganic matrix supplies no methyl donor.
MeHg.jurisdictions_checked: EU (Reg (EU) 1935/2004 framework + Annex I material families; Reg (EU) 10/2011 Annex II element list, as amended by 2016/1416 and 2020/1245); UK (retained Reg 10/2011); US (FDA food-contact substances, 21 CFR 174-190: no element migration ceiling for these elements); Codex (no food-contact-material standard); AU-NZ (FSANZ Food Standards Code 1.4.3 and 3.2.2: no element migration ceiling); Canada (Food and Drugs Act s.4 / letter-of-no-objection route, no numeric element migration ceiling); Hong Kong (Cap 132 subsidiary legislation: food limits only).
